title: Find which services slow down boot
summary: Shows how long the last startup took and which services and units took the longest to start. Use it when your Linux computer takes too long to start and you want to find the cause.

aliases.text: why is linux boot so slow
what slows down startup on linux
which service makes linux boot slow
ubuntu boot slow what is delaying

steps.explain: Show the total time of the last startup and how it is split between firmware, bootloader, kernel and system services (userspace). A big userspace number means the services are the place to look.
List the services and other units that took the longest to start, slowest first. The first lines are the usual suspects, but a slow service that runs in the background may not delay your desktop.
steps.expect: Lines with a time first and a unit name last, for example '4.210s NetworkManager-wait-online.service'.

alternatives.explain: Show the full list instead of the first 15 lines. The list can be long.

steps.explain: Show the chain of units that had to finish before the slow ones could start. A '@' value is when a unit became active and a '+' value is how long it took.
steps.expect: A tree of unit names, each with '@' and '+' times. The slowest unit in the chain is the one that delays startup.

alternatives.explain: Show the chain for one unit, for example one from the blame list. Replace <UNIT> with its name.

placeholders.name: UNIT
placeholders.description: Name of a systemd unit, for example one from the blame list

warnings: These numbers describe only the last startup. Reboot and run the commands again to compare.
